settings.title: Settings

adminTokensPanel.warning: These are installation-wide credentials. Treat them like root keys — anyone holding one can administer this hub, so revoke it the moment it leaks.

settings.mcp: Give an agent control of your fleet
settings.updates.blurb: Stable releases are checksum-verified, tested before replacement, and keep one previous version ready for rollback.
settings.updates.standaloneHint: This is a standalone/debug run. It can check releases, but automatic replacement is enabled after installing initagent as a background service. You can also run initagent update manually.
settings.updates.installStarted: Verified update is installing. The hub will restart automatically.
settings.updates.rollbackStarted: Previous version is being restored. The hub will restart automatically.
settings.updates.lastChecked: Last checked {{ago}} · managed agents retry automatically and update to the hub release.
settings.tokens.intro: For the initagent fleet CLI and the MCP server — this is how your coding agents get hands on the fleet. A token never exceeds your own permissions, and it stops working the moment you leave the organization it names.
settings.tokens.noMembershipHint: A token acts as a person inside an organization, and this session belongs to none. Create an organization first, or sign in with an account that is a member of one.
settings.tokens.dangerousHint: Running a command is not reading data. Anything holding one of these can execute code on the machines in scope.
settings.tokens.revokeConfirm: Revoke this token? Anything using it will lose access.
settings.presets.hint: One-click commands in the Launch dialog. Add your favorite agents.
settings.mcp.intro: Run a coding agent on any machine with the initagent binary and an API token, and it can see every connector, launch worker agents, read their output, and steer them. For Claude Code:
settings.mcp.thenAsk: Then ask it things like “launch claude in ~/projects/api on the homelab box and have it fix the failing tests.”
settings.mcp.scopesHint: An agent needs the connector, task and terminal scopes to do that, plus exec:fleet.connector if you want it running commands directly. If a tool comes back refused, the hub names the scope the token is missing — mint a new one with it rather than widening the old.
settings.mcp.remoteIntro: Any client that supports remote MCP connectors can drive your fleet over HTTPS. Add this endpoint and paste an API token as the Bearer credential:
settings.mcp.remoteWarning: ⚠️ This is a remote shell — the tools run commands and write files on your connectors. Only expose it over HTTPS (--tls-domain or a TLS proxy), and treat the API token like an SSH key. Revoke it above if it leaks.

setup.title: Prepare a coding machine from one place.
setup.subtitle: Install the major coding agents, open their secure sign-in flows, and add private remote access without moving auth files between computers.
setup.fxBuiltIn: fx control plane is built in
setup.fxHint: Sign in once from Code. The embedded fx runtime stays in your browser and routes work to any project node, so fx itself does not need to be installed or authenticated on every PC.
setup.agentPackHint: One setup terminal installs Codex, Claude Code, and Gemini CLI using their official distribution paths.
setup.legacySignInTitle: Why legacy agent sign-in still opens once per machine
setup.legacySignInHint: Codex, Claude, and Gemini store device credentials in their own protected local storage. LiveAgent starts each official login flow and keeps it visible in a remote terminal, but never copies those private tokens into the hub database. The built-in fx workspace above is the one-login path across nodes.
setup.noOnlineMachinesHint: Connect a connector first, then return here to prepare it.

models.title: Models
models.subtitle: The model registry of this installation: what each box's persona, worker, embedding and speech resolve to. The hub pins provenance only — it holds no weights.
models.registryHint: One pin per model and quantisation. The digest is the BLAKE3 of the pinned artifact — empty means unverified.
models.assignmentsHint: What each purpose resolves to when a box carries no override of its own. Only verified models are assignable.
models.orgHint: The Hugging Face namespace — the part of the repo id before the slash.
models.hfSearchHint: Search the Hugging Face catalogue and pin one of a repo's GGUF quants. You still fill the id and digest before saving.
models.noQuants: No GGUF files in this repo.
models.noQuantsHint: This repo has no GGUF files — you can still pin it with an empty quant.
models.suggestedPurposeHint: Read from the model card's task — change it if the pin serves another purpose.
models.idHint: The pin key — e.g. qwen3.5-4b-q4_k_m. Immutable after creation.
models.sourceHint: The Hugging Face repo@rev the weights are pinned to.
models.quantHint: The GGUF quantisation; empty for non-GGUF models.
models.digestHint: The BLAKE3 of the pinned artifact. Empty means unverified — compute it and fill it before assigning.
models.overrideHint: A per-box pin shadows the factory assignment. Clearing it falls back to the factory.
models.clearOverrideConfirm: Clear this override? The purpose falls back to the factory assignment.
models.confirmDeleteMessage: The pin goes away. A model still referenced by an assignment or a box override cannot be deleted.
